Readable sources only give period words for the sanctuary (PHRC: in use from 'the archaic period'; Swedish expedition summary: in use from late in the Cypro-Archaic period) or dates of single objects; the one year for its foundation (Gjerstad: about 500 BC) is on JSTOR, which the checker cannot read.

The reserve was declared in 1994 to protect woodland and contains several separate sites of different dates (Horvat Midras from the 10th century BCE, burial caves of the Late Bronze and Iron Ages at Hurvat Lavnin, Second Temple villages); no source gives one start for the reserve as a site, so a single year would be arbitrary.

The consortium page for the Puente romano de la Alcantarilla gives only its position on the right bank of the Guadiana on the Camino de Esparragalejo, without any coordinates, and no independent source could be found that prints a point for this bridge; the stored point therefore stays unsourced.
No readable source prints a point for Kunturmarka (Condormarca), Paucartambo District, Pasco: Wikipedia and Wikidata give none.
No source found dates Kunturmarka in Pasco; Wikipedia gives no date.
The Danubian Limes is a frontier running through seven countries; neither Wikipedia (en, de) nor its Wikidata item gives a coordinate for it, so no source point can be quoted.
No readable page prints a point for the Early Roman House of Nea Paphos; the Wikipedia and University of Warsaw pages name it only as one excavated building of the city.
The only page that dates the house is a scanned Polish Archaeology in the Mediterranean report whose text the checker cannot read; readable pages name the house without a date.
No readable page is about the Early Roman House itself; the pages found cover the whole city or an excavation season, and the only one that describes the house is a scanned PDF.

Spanish Wikipedia describes a mix of a defensive village or pucara, over 300 chullpa towers and a lower village; no readable source states one type of site for Laqaya as a whole in a quotable English or exact-type wording, so no single canonical type is attested.

Sources date only the Late Classic kingdom (AD 600-900) and say the dynasty flourished about 200 years, disintegrating by AD 800; none states when the site was founded or first occupied, and the earlier-occupied periphery is undated.
No readable source dates the start of Huankarán itself; the Tantamayo-valley date range (10th-14th centuries) is given for the region's sites as a class, not for this site.

Turkish Wikipedia puts the first settlement of Sidyma in the Iron Age, which is a period word and not a date, and it states expressly that the city was founded in the Lycian period but that there is no definite information about the year of foundation (kurulus yilina dair kesin bilgi olmadigini). Its oldest document, of 425 BC, attests the city rather than founding it. No source gives a dated start, so the field stays empty and the site goes to the owner's list.

No source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of the Ushnu of Pachitea, Umari, Huánuco. The Spanish article gives only its location and altitude, and the cited national register record (cod_Ficha=2922) no longer resolves to the record itself - the URL now returns the ministry's general page, so it cannot be quoted.

The Megalithic Portal point (20.9, -89.9) is rated accuracy 1 (nearest town) and the page itself says 'The location listed if for Merida. The location of this cave system is unknown to us.' NBC News and the Institute of Maya Studies newsletter give no coordinates, so no source gives the labyrinth's own point.

The English Wikipedia article says only that Chitinamit dates from the Early Classic through to the Late Postclassic periods. Those are period words without a year, century or millennium, so no source dates the start of the site and the field stays empty.

No source prints a coordinate pair for Inka Murata itself: the English Wikipedia article has none, Wikidata has no P625, and the pages found only place it in the community of Escara (Litoral Province, Oruro); the village point would not be the site's own point.

No source gives a date for the start of Inka Murata: Wikipedia and Law 3833 only name the site and its adjacent chullpas, and a press piece dates the chullpa tradition of Escara in general (13th-14th centuries), which is a range for a class of monuments, not this site.

No readable source prints a point for the Umm es-Sawan gypsum quarry itself: QuarryScapes, the Geological Survey of Norway paper, Archiqoo and Wikipedia describe its position only in words (about 20 km north-east of Widan el-Faras, Northern Faiyum), and the only coordinates found belong to the wider Gebel Qatrani area.

No source prints a point for Tampukancha in a readable form: the only page that carries one (Esperanto Wikipedia) writes it 13° 27' 51" S, 72° 15' 25" U, where the western hemisphere is the Esperanto letter U, not a signed decimal or N/S/E/W pair, so the stored point stands unsourced and the site goes to the owner.
No source dates the start of Tampukancha; the articles call it an Incan religious centre without a year, and no excavation report or register record with a date was found.

No source dates the Stairhaven Broch. The Megalithic Portal record calls it an 'iron age broch' and the linked pages describe the hamlet of Stairhaven, but no page gives a year, a century or a millennium for the monument's construction. A period word alone does not date the start, so the field stays empty.

The one source that describes the monument, the Megalithic Portal record, types it as 'Broch or Nuraghe' and calls it a broch; no source about Stairhaven itself uses the word that a canonical type would require (fort, fortification, tower, castle, mound, earthwork, scheduled monument). A broch is not one of the canonical types, and the other pages found for the name describe the hamlet, not an ancient monument, so the field stays empty rather than being stretched to a generic type.
No source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of Ayamachay; the rock-art survey only calls it late pre-Columbian, a period word without a date.

The Turkish Wikipedia article on Perge describes the Sütunlu Cadde only in plan terms ('Akropol eteğinde çeşme(nympheum) ile yerleşim arasında uzanır. Ortasında 2 m. genişliğinde bir su kanalı caddeyi ikiye ayırır.') and gives no year, century or millennium for its start, so the field stays empty.

No source gives a year, century or millennium for the building of the Yongin Wangsanli dolmens. The English article, the Korea Heritage Service record and the Gyeonggi heritage institute record date them only to the Bronze Age (청동기시대), a period word without a date, so the field stays empty.

Wikipedia gives only 'Iron Age'; Historic England's scheduling gives the eighth to fifth centuries BC and the Exmoor HER gives the generic Iron Age span 800 BC - 42 AD, both class-wide ranges for slight univallate hillforts / the period, not a date for this enclosure (the HER even calls it only 'probably prehistoric' and 'Most probably a non-defensive Iron Age settlement').

No source I can quote dates the start of this site. The Turkish Culture and Tourism Ministry's Mersin page on castles describes the Toroslar Kızlar Kalesi (Kızlar Kalesi-Manastır) only as a monastery on a hill slope with an 18-line Armenian inscription surviving, without a year, century or millennium; the Wikipedia article Kızlar Castle in fact describes the differently placed castle of Çavuşlu near Tarsus (4th century AD), so it cannot be used for this point.
